text.p: Dutch brokerage Van der Hoop Effektenbank and merchant bank Bangert Pontier lowered on Wednesday their ratings on food and biotechnology group Gist-Brocades.
Bangert Pontier cut its recommendation to Sell from Buy, and Van der Hoop now sees Gist-Brocades' stock as a Hold, down from its previous Buy rating.
Both research departments gave Tuesday's warning by Gist-Brocades as the reason for their downgrades.
"The profit warning that Gist-Brocades gave yesterday came totally unexpected," Van der Hoop said in a report.
The brokerage added that Gist-Brocades said in February it saw clearly higher 1997 net profits before one-off items.
This was repeated at least twice by the company's chief executive, and a Gist-Brocades spokesman confirmed this as recently as June 9, Van der Hoop said.
It cut its 1997 earnings per share estimate to 3.80 guilders from 4.65 and the 1998 estimate to 4.20 from 5.10 guilders.

Gist-Brocades said on Tuesday its expected 1997 profit fall was due to penicillin prices having reached historic lows. But Van der Hoop said the fact that the company had apparently been unaware of the impact of this on June 9 was "disappointing".
Bangert Pontier said it had spoken with the company recently and that Gist-Brocades had then given no indication that penicillin prices had dropped so sharply.

"We feel that Gist-Brocades should either have been capable of making a more accurate prediction of the penicillin prices when it made its (previous) 1997 forecast, or at the very least should have noted the decline sooner during the current year," Bangert Pontier said in its research note.
The merchant bank also cut its EPS estimates for future years ahead. Earnings per share for 1997 were now seen at 3.72 guilders, down from a previous estimate of 4.46.
The 1998 and 1999 forecasts were cut to 3.99 and 4.20 guilders, down from previous estimates of 5.01 and 5.47 guilders respectively.
"We feel the company has let the shareholders down badly," Bangert Pontier said, adding that Gist-Brocades' focus on sales volumes "at all costs" might hurt penicillin prices further.
"For these reasons, we reduce our EPS estimates and downgrade the stock to Sell," the bank said.
